variant.stem_override: A 45-year-old woman presents to clinic with 8 weeks of bilateral symmetric polyarthritis involving the metacarpophalangeal (MCP) joints, proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joints, and wrists. She reports >2 hours of morning stiffness that improves with activity. She has a history of an uncomplicated appendectomy at age 20. Exam shows synovitis (boggy, tender, mildly swollen) of multiple MCP and PIP joints and both wrists; the distal interphalangeal joints are spared. There is no skin rash, no nail pitting, no sicca symptoms, no preceding gastrointestinal or genitourinary infection, no Raynaud phenomenon. Labs: rheumatoid factor 80 IU/mL (positive); anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (anti-CCP) 250 U/mL (markedly positive); ESR 65 mm/h, CRP 32 mg/L. Hand and wrist X-rays show marginal erosions of several MCP joints and periarticular osteopenia. ANA negative; CBC normal.
variant.rationale_for_variant: A single incidental fact — a remote uncomplicated appendectomy — was inserted as a distractor. It has no bearing on inflammatory polyarthritis, serology, or acute-phase reactants; the ACR/EULAR score remains 8/10, so rheumatoid arthritis (A) is still the answer.
